chunks: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-'Ubaydi, from Durust, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Abi al-Hasan عليه السلام, he said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم entered upon 'A'ishah while she had placed her ewer in the sun. He said: “O Humayra', what is this?” She said: “I am washing my head and my body.” He said: “Do not do it again, for it causes leprosy.”
So it is to be understood as indicating a kind of karahah (dislike) rather than prohibition.

key_terms.أَغْسِلُ: I wash; referring here to washing the head and body
key_terms.الشَّمْسِ: the sun, by which the water was heated
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislike or reprehensibility in legal usage

ai.seo_question: Is using water heated by the sun for washing prohibited in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report addresses the use of water heated by the sun for washing the body. The final statement clarifies that the report is understood to indicate karahah (dislike), not prohibition, making it relevant to fiqh discussions of ritual purity and permissible usage of water.
